title: the four mahavakyas — prajnanam brahma
tomorrow: how close is the sacred? two old books answer.

segments.voice: Yesterday, the four mahavakyas at their widest: gods, elephants and sprouts, all guided by the knowing, the world's eye. Today, the text's other list, the one inside a person.
screen: `THE WORLD HAS KNOWING FOR ITS EYE.`

segments.voice: The week before a big change, the inside gets loud. Excited at breakfast, snappy by lunch, wide awake at two in the morning, wanting everything and nothing. None of it looks like a holy list. Yet just before its crowded window on the world, the Aitareya Upanishad makes a list of exactly this, everything that goes on inside a person. And it puts desire and will on it, right beside wisdom.
screen: `EXCITED. SNAPPY. AWAKE AT TWO.` → `A LIST OF THE INSIDE.` → `DESIRE AND WILL, BESIDE WISDOM.`

segments.voice: Having asked which one is the self, the Aitareya lists the inner powers. The heart and the mind. Awareness, understanding, discernment. Wisdom, insight, steadiness. Thought, reflection, drive. Memory, intention, purpose. Life, desire, will. Translators render these words in different ways, because the Sanskrit has many overlapping words for knowing. Then the text says one thing about the whole list: all of these are names of prajnana, the knowing. Look at what made the list. Not only the calm, admirable things. Desire is there. Drive is there. Will, the part of a person that insists, is there. The text doesn't sort the inner life into clean and messy, keep this, throw out that. It calls each one a name of the same knowing. That changes how a hard week reads. A restless mind, a memory that still stings, a want that won't let go: in this passage, each is the knowing at work, under another name. Not the whole of it. A name of it. This isn't permission to act on every want; the Upanishad isn't giving advice here at all. It's drawing a map. And on that map, nothing inside a person falls outside the knowing that the next lines call Brahman.
screen: `HEART, MIND, MEMORY, WILL.` · `ALL NAMES OF PRAJNANA.` · `NOT SORTED INTO CLEAN AND MESSY.` · `A MAP, NOT PERMISSION.` · then, large: `EVEN A WANT IS A NAME OF THE KNOWING.`

segments.voice: Sit upright with one hand resting on your chest. As each thought or feeling arrives, a plan, a worry, a want, give it a plain name from the list, memory, desire, will, and let it pass under your hand. Each one is a name; the knowing that names it stays.
The four mahavakyas, and prajnanam brahma from the inside: heart, memory, desire and will, all names of the one knowing.
Your line: the four mahavakyas — prajnanam brahma. Even a want is a name of the knowing. Day 1741 is in.

howItsDone: Students of the Aitareya read this list slowly with a teacher, and some return to it in meditation, naming each movement of the mind as a name of prajnana.

prajnana.meaning: knowing; that by which anything is seen or heard

prajnanam brahma.meaning: the knowing is Brahman; one of the great sayings

mahavakyas.meaning: the great sayings, gathered by tradition from the Upanishads
